original_question: Extend the geodesic and Hamiltonian Euler-Arnold framework from Lie groups to Lie groupoids in a way that also covers elasticity theory, not only multiphase and vortex-sheet fluid models.
target_in_paper: Section 2.2, Problem 2: "Extend the geodesic and Hamiltonian descriptions of the Euler-Arnold equations on Lie groupoids to problems of elasticity theory." ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is close to the paper’s actual open problem: it correctly centers the geodesic/Hamiltonian Euler-Arnold viewpoint, the passage from Lie-group-based fluid geometry to a Lie-groupoid setting, and the goal of reaching elasticity theory rather than staying only with previously treated fluid examples. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))
missing_details: The paper does not pose a general new extension from Lie groups to Lie groupoids; it says that this extension has already been achieved for incompressible multiphase fluids, generalized flows, and vortex sheets, and then asks for the elasticity-theory analogue. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))

The nearby context includes one fluid class omitted in your draft: generalized flows, i.e. multiphase fluids with a continuum of phases. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))

To be stand-alone, the question should mention the local geometric setup used in the surrounding paragraph: a Riemannian manifold M, phase densities ρ_j ∈ C∞(M), phase velocities v_j ∈ Vect(M), common pressure p ∈ C∞(M), the equations ∂_t v_j + v_j·∇v_j = -∇p and ∂_tρ_j + div(ρ_j v_j)=0, and the total incompressibility constraint Σ_j ρ_j = 1. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))

The known geometric structure is more specific than 'Lie groupoids' in the abstract: the paper points to Lie groupoids of multiphase volume-preserving diffeomorphisms, their Lie algebroids, and an L^2-type right-invariant (source-wise) metric whose geodesics give the fluid solutions. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))

The elasticity target is intentionally broad in the paper: it says only 'problems of elasticity theory' and cites [65], [82], and [98], without imposing a constitutive law, boundary regime, or a single canonical elastic PDE, so adding such hypotheses would go beyond the text. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))

The statement is programmatic rather than algebraic or asymptotic: the paper introduces no ambient ring/field, homogeneity, degree bounds, nilpotency condition, or 'for all sufficiently large' quantifier here. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))
refined_question: Can one develop, for problems of elasticity theory, an analogue of the Lie-groupoid Euler-Arnold framework already available for incompressible multiphase fluids, generalized flows, and vortex sheets by identifying the appropriate Lie groupoid of elastic configurations and its Lie algebroid, together with a geodesic and Hamiltonian formulation analogous to the known L^2-type right-invariant (source-wise) metric picture on Lie groupoids of multiphase volume-preserving diffeomorphisms? ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))
justification: This rewrite follows the nearest official formulation in the paper, namely Problem 2 of Section 2.2, rather than broadening to neighboring questions. The surrounding paragraph first records what is already known: Lie-groupoid descriptions for multiphase fluids, generalized flows, and vortex sheets, including Lie algebroids, Hamiltonian interpretations, and an L^2-type source-wise metric whose geodesics are the corresponding motions; it then singles out elasticity theory as the next application domain. The adjacent Problem 3 is different: it asks for sectional/Ricci curvature, conjugate points, and related differential-geometric data for the existing groupoid metric, not for an elasticity formulation. Since the paper does not specify extra constitutive assumptions for elasticity, the faithful refinement keeps that level of generality and does not invent additional hypotheses. ([math.toronto.edu](https://www.math.toronto.edu/khesin/papers/Problems_in_GHD_ARMA.pdf))
